5	---
6	
7	## 1. Representation: what the graph actually is
8	
9	**Recommendation: a causal Bayesian network over time-ordered, resolvable binary propositions — computed as a BN, displayed as a DAG, narrated as a tree.**
10	
11	- **Event/scenario tree.** Enumerates paths — exactly the "multiverse" metaphor — but is exponential and unfactored: editing one event means editing every branch containing it. Fatal for a tool whose core gesture is *edit one node*. Use a tree only as a *derived view* (top-k paths through the DAG).
12	- **Argument map.** Carries justification, not probability; composition is undefined. Keep it as an *evidence annotation* on nodes and edges, never as the thing that computes.
13	- **Influence diagram.** A BN plus decision and utility nodes. Since the final stage is "a thesis you can trade on", the trade *is* a decision and P&L *is* a utility — a small, high-value increment, but only at the end.
14	- **Causal BN / SCM.** Factorises, supports local edits, supports `do()`. The core.
15	
16	**What "modify an event" means formally.** Pearl's ladder ([Pearl 2018](https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r481.pdf)) forces a distinction the UI must make visible, because the three operations give *different numbers*:
17	
18	1. **Observe** `X = x` (rung 1): conditioning. Propagates downstream *and upstream* — learning "Iran was struck" raises the probability of its own causes and explains away rivals. This is "suppose we learn that…".
19	2. **Intervene** `do(X = x)` (rung 2): cut `X`'s incoming edges, then condition. No upstream revision. This is "force it on, regardless of why".
20	3. **Counterfactual** (rung 3): "in *this* world, what if Iran had *also* been struck?" For *future* nodes this is just rung 2 on a partially-observed world, which is fine. True rung 3 — rewriting an already-resolved event while holding the world's idiosyncrasy fixed — needs a functional form plus persistent exogenous noise. A CPT-only BN cannot do it.
21	
22	**On honesty.** With LLM-elicited structure you can claim rungs 1 and 2 *relative to the stated model* — never "this is the causal structure of the world", always "this is what you and the model asserted; here is what follows". The optimistic result ([Kıcıman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00050)) and the pessimistic one ([Zečević et al., *Causal Parrots*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13067)) agree the model is *recalling* causal claims from text, not discovering them. Fine for a hypothesis generator — but the tool's epistemic warrant then comes from auditability, not from the model.
23	
24	Rung 3 is worth one cheap concession: a **latent-threshold link** (logistic or noisy-OR, below) gives you a canonical SCM for free — independent latent inhibitor bits — so abduction→action→prediction is computable. Do it, but label the output "counterfactual (model-dependent)"; the canonical form is a modelling choice, not a fact.
25	
26	**Edge typing is mandatory.** LLMs emit definitional and evidential edges alongside causal ones ("oil spikes → energy equities rally" is near-tautological co-movement; "tanker rates rise" is a *symptom* of disruption, not a cause). Tag each edge `causal | definitional | evidential`; only `causal` edges may be cut by `do()`. This one field prevents a class of nonsense.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## 2. Parameterisation with few numbers
31	
32	Full CPTs are `2^k` rows per node — at `k = 4`, 16 numbers, elicited from a model that will produce non-monotone, mutually incoherent rows. Don't.
33	
34	- **Leaky noisy-OR**: `k + 1` numbers. Assumes *independence of causal influence*, all causes *generative*, OR-combination. It **cannot express inhibition** or **synergy** (two causes needed together). Both are ubiquitous in finance: "already priced in", "OPEC offsets the shortfall", "the Fed cuts to absorb the shock" are inhibitory. Noisy-OR as the *sole* link type is the most common rigor failure in tools like this.
35	- **Noisy-MAX**: ordered multi-state generalisation — right for "oil: down / flat / up / spike". 36	- **Ranked nodes / weighted-mean** ([Fenton, Neil & Caballero 2007](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/3297767_Using_Ranked_Nodes_to_Model_Qualitative_Judgments_in_Bayesian_Networks)): hundreds of CPT cells from a weight per parent plus a variance. Good for ordinal severity scales.
37	- **Logistic / log-odds link**: `logit P(child) = b0 + Σ wᵢ·xᵢ`. Also `k + 1` numbers; `b0` is the base rate with no causes active, each `wᵢ` a **signed** log-odds ratio.
38	
39	**Recommendation: signed log-odds as the default, with leaky noisy-OR and noisy-AND per node.** It handles inhibition, which noisy-OR cannot; elicitation is in odds ratios ("~3× more likely"), which forecasters can produce; each edge's contribution is `wᵢ` in bits, so the inspector gets "this edge moved the target +1.2 bits" free; and it is a threshold model with a logistic latent, so rung-3 abduction works. 40	
41	Remaining failure modes: **double counting correlated paths** (two parents driven by the same unmodelled cause are treated as independent evidence — lint for shared ancestors and semantic overlap); **missing common causes** (an edge silently absorbs confounding, so `do()` on it is wrong — require a one-line mechanism per edge, since an author who cannot state one probably has confounding); **saturation** (clip and warn past ~0.99).
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 3. Eliciting and calibrating LLM probabilities
46	
47	The empirical picture: scaffolded, retrieval-augmented LLMs approach crowd-aggregate accuracy ([Halawi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563)), and LLM *ensembles* are statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd on small question sets ([Schoenegger et al., Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adp1528)) — but on a leakage-free, continuously-refreshed benchmark superforecasters still beat the best LLM by Brier 0.068 vs 0.119 ([ForecastBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19839)), several times the GPT-4→GPT-4o gap. The popular read ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)) is that scaffolds are worth about a model generation and finance-adjacent questions are where AI does relatively *best*. Encouraging — but the scaffold is doing the work, not the model.
48	
49	Elicitation protocol, in priority order:
50	
51	1. **Base rate before narrative.** Elicit the reference class and its historical frequency in a *separate call that has not seen the scenario*, then adjust in a second call. Merging them invites representativeness: a vivid chain scores high because it is a good *story*.
52	2. **Elicit conditionals, never joints.** Ask for `P(B|A)` and `P(B|¬A)`; compute the rest. Humans and LLMs both violate the conjunction rule — a detailed conjunction is judged *more* likely than its own conjunct ([Tversky & Kahneman 1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunction_fallacy)). A five-step chain at 0.8 per step is 0.33, and the model will call it "very likely" if allowed.
53	3. **Sample k ≥ 5 times** across prompt variants and ideally two model families, then **aggregate by geometric mean of odds** ([summary](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/sMjcjnnpoAQCcedL2/when-pooling-forecasts-use-the-geometric-mean-of-odds)). **Keep the spread**: dispersion across independent elicitations is a defensible first-order estimate of that parameter's uncertainty, feeding §4 at zero extra cost.
54	4. **Do not extremize by default.** Extremizing helps for independent human forecasters ([discussion](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/biL94PKfeHmgHY6qe/principled-extremizing-of-aggregated-forecasts)), but LLM samples are highly correlated and chain errors compound multiplicatively. 55	5. **Correct known LLM pathologies**: RLHF pushes models toward confident-sounding outputs ([Taming Overconfidence in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09724)), and verbalized probabilities cluster on round numbers and avoid the tails. 56	
57	**Coherence checks to run automatically** (all cheap, all blocking):
58	
59	- Marginal consistency: `P(B) ≈ P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|¬A)P(¬A)` vs. a directly-elicited `P(B)`; flag >10pp divergence.
60	- Relevance: an edge is justified only if `P(B|A) ≠ P(B|¬A)`. Equal values → delete the edge.
61	- Symmetry of dependence: `P(B|A) > P(B)` iff `P(A|B) > P(A)`.
62	- Chain sanity: compare the model's *verbal* summary ("highly likely") against the computed number and show the conflict. This is the anti-conjunction-fallacy feature, and a genuinely good product moment.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 4. Uncertainty about uncertainty
67	
68	Ranked by value-per-hour:
69	
70	1. **Monte Carlo over parameters → a band, not a point.** Draw each parameter from its across-sample dispersion (§3.3) ~1,000 times and re-run inference. ~20 lines, and the strongest antidote to false precision: the band visibly widens with chain length, which is the honest lesson.

74	
75	**Skip imprecise probability / credal networks.** Interval propagation is exponential in practice, the intervals go vacuously wide, and no user can interpret them. Parameter MC captures ~90% of the honesty at ~5% of the cost.
76	
77	---

79	## 5. Ontology: what is an "event"
80	
81	A node is a **resolvable proposition**: unambiguous statement + time window + named resolution source. "Tensions escalate in the Gulf" fails. "US or Israeli kinetic strike on Iranian territory reported by ≥2 of {Reuters, AP, FT} before 2026-12-31" passes. Make it a first-class validator.
82	
83	Distinguish **event** (occurs within a window), **state** (holds over an interval) and **quantity** (a number). Financial targets are quantities and users trade *thresholds*, so represent quantities as an ordered, mutually-exclusive, exhaustive partition ("Brent settle: <$70 / $70–85 / $85–100 / ≥$100 on 2026-12-31") with noisy-MAX. Siblings must literally partition, or probabilities stop summing to 1.
84	
85	**Granularity rule:** one nameable mechanism per edge. No statable mechanism means a missing intermediate node. But resist infinite subdivision — each node is another elicited number and another place to double count.
86	
87	**Structural uncertainty is the dominant error term, and the leak is where it lives.** Every node's "no parents active" probability must be *elicited as a base rate*, never defaulted to zero; a zero leak asserts the LLM's cause list is exhaustive, which it never is. Disclose per graph that the computed number is a lower bound if the enumerated causes are only some of the causes.
88	
89	**Black swans** cannot be enumerated, so don't price them. 90	
91	---
92	
93	## 6. Scoring and auditability
94	
95	- **Provenance per node and edge**: source URLs with retrieval timestamps, model, prompt version, elicitation method, and the k raw samples *before* aggregation. Without the raw samples you cannot distinguish "the model was confident" from "the models disagreed and we averaged".
96	- **Immutable snapshots.** Every published chain is frozen and timestamped so it can be scored later. A forecast you can silently edit is not a forecast.
97	- **Proper scoring rules.** Brier for the user-facing calibration view; log score alongside, since it punishes confident errors — the failure mode that matters here. Always report a **skill score** relative to the elicited base rate; absolute Brier on easy questions flatters everyone.
98	- **Score sub-claims, not just the target.** A chain that lands the right answer through compensating errors must be flagged. Node-level scoring is what makes a chain falsifiable rather than merely narratable.
99	- **Publishing gate:** every node passes the clarity test, has a resolution date and source, and at least one resolves within the user's horizon. Surface the earliest-resolving, highest-VOI nodes as **tripwires**.
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 7. Inference
104	
105	At ≤30 binary nodes with hand-built sparse structure, treewidth is typically ≤6. **Exact enumeration** is trivially correct but fine only to ~20 nodes (`2^20` ≈ 1M) — and the parameter-MC loop in §4 multiplies that by 1,000. **Variable elimination** with min-fill ordering is ~150 lines, exact, deterministic and explains cleanly ("we summed out the nodes you didn't ask about"); this is what I would maintain. **Forward/logic sampling with `do()`** is the right *narrative* engine, because the multiverse view is literally sampled worlds: "of 10,000 simulated worlds where Hormuz opens and Iran is struck, 3,100 had Brent below $70" is a sentence users trust (downstream evidence needs likelihood weighting; keep evidence upstream where possible). Skip MCMC/Gibbs entirely.
106	
107	**Build both and assert they agree within MC error in a test** — the cheapest correctness guarantee in the system.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## (a) The minimal sound core a staff engineer would build
112	
113	1. **Node** = resolvable proposition (or ordered threshold partition of a quantity): statement, window, resolution source, base rate / leak, provenance.
114	2. **Edge** = signed log-odds weight (default) + mechanism clause + type (`causal | definitional | evidential`) + provenance. Per-node link choice: logistic, leaky noisy-OR, noisy-AND, noisy-MAX.
115	3. **Time-ordered DAG** with cycle and time-order validation (no effect before its cause).
116	4. **Three distinct, differently-labelled operators**: `observe`, `do` (causal edges only), structural edit. Optional rung-3 via logistic-latent abduction, labelled "model-dependent".
117	5. **Inference**: VE for numbers, forward sampling for narrative, agreement test between them.
118	6. **Elicitation service**: base-rate-first, conditionals-only, k samples, geometric mean of odds, dispersion retained as parameter uncertainty.
119	7. **Coherence auditor** (§3), blocking on failure.
120	8. **Uncertainty panel**: parameter-MC band, tornado, edge-ablation badges, VOI tripwire list.
121	9. **Final stage**: one decision node + P&L mapping → return distribution, P(stop hit), P(target hit), expected value. The only place a point estimate is defensible.
122	10. **Scoring ledger**: frozen snapshots, node-level resolution, Brier + log score + skill vs. base rate, per-model calibration curve.
123	
124	## (b) Eight rigor traps, each with a concrete test
125	
126	1. **Conditioning sold as intervention.** *Test:* toggle a mid-chain node via the "what if" control and watch its *parents'* probabilities. If they move, it is conditioning. Both operations are legitimate; being unable to tell which one you got is not.
127	2. **Path-multiplication instead of inference.** *Test:* build a diamond (A→B→D, A→C→D) and compare the tool's `P(D|A)` against hand-enumerated exact inference. Multiplying along paths double counts A and gives a different number.
128	3. **Non-exhaustive / non-exclusive outcomes.** *Test:* create siblings "oil up / flat / down"; check the displayed probabilities sum to 1 and that no single sampled world contains both "up" and "down".
129	4. **Zero leak.** *Test:* set every parent of a node false. If `P(node) = 0`, the model asserts the LLM's cause list is exhaustive. Confirm the leak was elicited, not defaulted.
130	5. **LLM-stated joint probabilities.** *Test:* inspect the prompts — is the model ever asked for the probability of a whole path or of the target given the story? Is the displayed path probability computed or generated? Re-run one edge twice; if the stored number moves, it is a single unaggregated sample.
131	6. **Narrative swamping the base rate.** *Test:* build a chain ending in a rare, documented event ("S&P 500 falls >20% in a quarter", historically a few percent). With no assumptions applied, is the unconditional endpoint anywhere near that? If it reads 30%, the story is driving the number.
132	7. **False precision / no pivot surfacing.** *Test:* move one edge from `P(B|A) = 0.6` to `0.45` and see whether the headline conclusion flips. If it does and the UI never flagged that edge as load-bearing, the audit story is broken. Any figure past two significant digits is theatre.
133	8. **Non-falsifiable nodes.** *Test:* sample 10 generated nodes and apply the clarity test — date, source, judgement-free resolution — and record the failure fraction. Then check whether any resolved outcome is written back and scored. A tool that never scores itself cannot claim rigor.

135	## (c) What NOT to build

137	- **Causal discovery from data** and **do-calculus identification machinery.** No dataset; the structure is stipulated. Backdoor adjustment on an elicited graph is ceremony.
138	- **Credal sets / imprecise probability.** Costly, vacuous, uninterpretable.
139	- **General hybrid continuous BNs.** Thresholded quantities plus noisy-MAX cover the financial cases.
140	- **Dynamic Bayesian networks / time-step simulation.** Use dated nodes; a DBN is a different product.
141	- **Fitting CPTs from market data.** A multi-month project with its own backtest-overfitting failure modes.
142	- **Large auto-generated graphs (100+ nodes).** The value is the audit, not the sprawl. Cap near 30.
143	- **MCMC/Gibbs, junction-tree compilation, approximate-inference research.** Unneeded at this scale.
144	- **Rung-3 claims about resolved history** without an explicit SCM and a "model-dependent" label.

- **Ranked nodes / weighted-mean** ([Fenton, Neil & Caballero 2007](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/3297767_Using_Ranked_Nodes_to_Model_Qualitative_Judgments_in_Bayesian_Networks)): hundreds of CPT cells from a weight per parent plus a variance. Good for ordinal severity scales.
- **Logistic / log-odds link**: `logit P(child) = b0 + Σ wᵢ·xᵢ`. Also `k + 1` numbers; `b0` is the base rate with no causes active, each `wᵢ` a **signed** log-odds ratio.

**Recommendation: signed log-odds as the default, with leaky noisy-OR and noisy-AND per node.** It handles inhibition, which noisy-OR cannot; elicitation is in odds ratios ("~3× more likely"), which forecasters can produce; each edge's contribution is `wᵢ` in bits, so the inspector gets "this edge moved the target +1.2 bits" free; and it is a threshold model with a logistic latent, so rung-3 abduction works. Keep **noisy-AND**, because use case (1) — "is there a *reasonable chain* from A to B?" — is conjunctive, and an OR-ish default makes every chain look strong.

Remaining failure modes: **double counting correlated paths** (two parents driven by the same unmodelled cause are treated as independent evidence — lint for shared ancestors and semantic overlap); **missing common causes** (an edge silently absorbs confounding, so `do()` on it is wrong — require a one-line mechanism per edge, since an author who cannot state one probably has confounding); **saturation** (clip and warn past ~0.99).

---

## 3. Eliciting and calibrating LLM probabilities

The empirical picture: scaffolded, retrieval-augmented LLMs approach crowd-aggregate accuracy ([Halawi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563)), and LLM *ensembles* are statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd on small question sets ([Schoenegger et al., Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adp1528)) — but on a leakage-free, continuously-refreshed benchmark superforecasters still beat the best LLM by Brier 0.068 vs 0.119 ([ForecastBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19839)), several times the GPT-4→GPT-4o gap. The popular read ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)) is that scaffolds are worth about a model generation and finance-adjacent questions are where AI does relatively *best*. Encouraging — but the scaffold is doing the work, not the model.

Elicitation protocol, in priority order:

1. **Base rate before narrative.** Elicit the reference class and its historical frequency in a *separate call that has not seen the scenario*, then adjust in a second call. Merging them invites representativeness: a vivid chain scores high because it is a good *story*.
2. **Elicit conditionals, never joints.** Ask for `P(B|A)` and `P(B|¬A)`; compute the rest. Humans and LLMs both violate the conjunction rule — a detailed conjunction is judged *more* likely than its own conjunct ([Tversky & Kahneman 1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunction_fallacy)). A five-step chain at 0.8 per step is 0.33, and the model will call it "very likely" if allowed.
3. **Sample k ≥ 5 times** across prompt variants and ideally two model families, then **aggregate by geometric mean of odds** ([summary](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/sMjcjnnpoAQCcedL2/when-pooling-forecasts-use-the-geometric-mean-of-odds)). **Keep the spread**: dispersion across independent elicitations is a defensible first-order estimate of that parameter's uncertainty, feeding §4 at zero extra cost.
4. **Do not extremize by default.** Extremizing helps for independent human forecasters ([discussion](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/biL94PKfeHmgHY6qe/principled-extremizing-of-aggregated-forecasts)), but LLM samples are highly correlated and chain errors compound multiplicatively. Here it manufactures confidence.
5. **Correct known LLM pathologies**: RLHF pushes models toward confident-sounding outputs ([Taming Overconfidence in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09724)), and verbalized probabilities cluster on round numbers and avoid the tails. Force explicit `<1%` / `>99%` options; add a per-model recalibration map once questions resolve.

**Coherence checks to run automatically** (all cheap, all blocking):

- Marginal consistency: `P(B) ≈ P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|¬A)P(¬A)` vs. a directly-elicited `P(B)`; flag >10pp divergence.
- Relevance: an edge is justified only if `P(B|A) ≠ P(B|¬A)`. Equal values → delete the edge.
- Symmetry of dependence: `P(B|A) > P(B)` iff `P(A|B) > P(A)`.
- Chain sanity: compare the model's *verbal* summary ("highly likely") against the computed number and show the conflict. This is the anti-conjunction-fallacy feature, and a genuinely good product moment.

---

## 4. Uncertainty about uncertainty

Ranked by value-per-hour:

1. **Monte Carlo over parameters → a band, not a point.** Draw each parameter from its across-sample dispersion (§3.3) ~1,000 times and re-run inference. ~20 lines, and the strongest antidote to false precision: the band visibly widens with chain length, which is the honest lesson.
2. **One-way sensitivity / tornado.** Perturb each parameter over its plausible range, rank by target movement ([Kjærulff & van der Gaag, as in GeNIe](https://support.bayesfusion.com/docs/GeNIe/bn_sensitivitybn.html)). `2 × #params` inferences — milliseconds here. Tells the user *which single number their thesis rests on*.
3. **Edge-ablation robustness.** Set each edge to no-effect and re-check whether the conclusion ("target > 60%") survives. A per-edge "load-bearing" badge is more useful to a trader than any interval.
4. **Value of information.** For each unresolved node, `ΔVar ≈ p(1−p)·(E[T|x] − E[T|¬x])²` ranks "what to watch next" — simultaneously a rigor feature and *the* product feature: the tripwire list.

**Skip imprecise probability / credal networks.** Interval propagation is exponential in practice, the intervals go vacuously wide, and no user can interpret them. Parameter MC captures ~90% of the honesty at ~5% of the cost.

---

## 5. Ontology: what is an "event"

A node is a **resolvable proposition**: unambiguous statement + time window + named resolution source. Apply Howard's **clarity/clairvoyance test** ([Howard 1988](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1539-6924.1988.tb01156.x); [summary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarity_test)) — a clairvoyant with all future newspapers must resolve it *without judgement*. "Tensions escalate in the Gulf" fails. "US or Israeli kinetic strike on Iranian territory reported by ≥2 of {Reuters, AP, FT} before 2026-12-31" passes. Make it a first-class validator.

Distinguish **event** (occurs within a window), **state** (holds over an interval) and **quantity** (a number). Financial targets are quantities and users trade *thresholds*, so represent quantities as an ordered, mutually-exclusive, exhaustive partition ("Brent settle: <$70 / $70–85 / $85–100 / ≥$100 on 2026-12-31") with noisy-MAX. Siblings must literally partition, or probabilities stop summing to 1.

**Granularity rule:** one nameable mechanism per edge. No statable mechanism means a missing intermediate node. But resist infinite subdivision — each node is another elicited number and another place to double count.

**Structural uncertainty is the dominant error term, and the leak is where it lives.** Every node's "no parents active" probability must be *elicited as a base rate*, never defaulted to zero; a zero leak asserts the LLM's cause list is exhaustive, which it never is. Disclose per graph that the computed number is a lower bound if the enumerated causes are only some of the causes.

**Black swans** cannot be enumerated, so don't price them. Two honest mechanisms: an optional **shock parent** on key nodes with small probability and large effect, pinned ON via `do()` in *stress* mode; and heavy-tailed magnitude on quantity nodes, so the P&L view reports conditional loss *given* the tail rather than only its probability. **The tool stresses tails; it does not predict them.**

---

## 6. Scoring and auditability

- **Provenance per node and edge**: source URLs with retrieval timestamps, model, prompt version, elicitation method, and the k raw samples *before* aggregation. Without the raw samples you cannot distinguish "the model was confident" from "the models disagreed and we averaged".
- **Immutable snapshots.** Every published chain is frozen and timestamped so it can be scored later. A forecast you can silently edit is not a forecast.
- **Proper scoring rules.** Brier for the user-facing calibration view; log score alongside, since it punishes confident errors — the failure mode that matters here. Always report a **skill score** relative to the elicited base rate; absolute Brier on easy questions flatters everyone.
- **Score sub-claims, not just the target.** A chain that lands the right answer through compensating errors must be flagged. Node-level scoring is what makes a chain falsifiable rather than merely narratable.
- **Publishing gate:** every node passes the clarity test, has a resolution date and source, and at least one resolves within the user's horizon. Surface the earliest-resolving, highest-VOI nodes as **tripwires**.

---

## 7. Inference

At ≤30 binary nodes with hand-built sparse structure, treewidth is typically ≤6. **Exact enumeration** is trivially correct but fine only to ~20 nodes (`2^20` ≈ 1M) — and the parameter-MC loop in §4 multiplies that by 1,000. **Variable elimination** with min-fill ordering is ~150 lines, exact, deterministic and explains cleanly ("we summed out the nodes you didn't ask about"); this is what I would maintain. **Forward/logic sampling with `do()`** is the right *narrative* engine, because the multiverse view is literally sampled worlds: "of 10,000 simulated worlds where Hormuz opens and Iran is struck, 3,100 had Brent below $70" is a sentence users trust (downstream evidence needs likelihood weighting; keep evidence upstream where possible). Skip MCMC/Gibbs entirely.

**Build both and assert they agree within MC error in a test** — the cheapest correctness guarantee in the system.

---

## (a) The minimal sound core a staff engineer would build

1. **Node** = resolvable proposition (or ordered threshold partition of a quantity): statement, window, resolution source, base rate / leak, provenance.
2. **Edge** = signed log-odds weight (default) + mechanism clause + type (`causal | definitional | evidential`) + provenance. Per-node link choice: logistic, leaky noisy-OR, noisy-AND, noisy-MAX.
3. **Time-ordered DAG** with cycle and time-order validation (no effect before its cause).
4. **Three distinct, differently-labelled operators**: `observe`, `do` (causal edges only), structural edit. Optional rung-3 via logistic-latent abduction, labelled "model-dependent".
5. **Inference**: VE for numbers, forward sampling for narrative, agreement test between them.
6. **Elicitation service**: base-rate-first, conditionals-only, k samples, geometric mean of odds, dispersion retained as parameter uncertainty.
7. **Coherence auditor** (§3), blocking on failure.
8. **Uncertainty panel**: parameter-MC band, tornado, edge-ablation badges, VOI tripwire list.
9. **Final stage**: one decision node + P&L mapping → return distribution, P(stop hit), P(target hit), expected value. The only place a point estimate is defensible.
10. **Scoring ledger**: frozen snapshots, node-level resolution, Brier + log score + skill vs. base rate, per-model calibration curve.

## (b) Eight rigor traps, each with a concrete test

1. **Conditioning sold as intervention.** *Test:* toggle a mid-chain node via the "what if" control and watch its *parents'* probabilities. If they move, it is conditioning. Both operations are legitimate; being unable to tell which one you got is not.
2. **Path-multiplication instead of inference.** *Test:* build a diamond (A→B→D, A→C→D) and compare the tool's `P(D|A)` against hand-enumerated exact inference. Multiplying along paths double counts A and gives a different number.
3. **Non-exhaustive / non-exclusive outcomes.** *Test:* create siblings "oil up / flat / down"; check the displayed probabilities sum to 1 and that no single sampled world contains both "up" and "down".
4. **Zero leak.** *Test:* set every parent of a node false. If `P(node) = 0`, the model asserts the LLM's cause list is exhaustive. Confirm the leak was elicited, not defaulted.
5. **LLM-stated joint probabilities.** *Test:* inspect the prompts — is the model ever asked for the probability of a whole path or of the target given the story? Is the displayed path probability computed or generated? Re-run one edge twice; if the stored number moves, it is a single unaggregated sample.
6. **Narrative swamping the base rate.** *Test:* build a chain ending in a rare, documented event ("S&P 500 falls >20% in a quarter", historically a few percent). With no assumptions applied, is the unconditional endpoint anywhere near that? If it reads 30%, the story is driving the number.
7. **False precision / no pivot surfacing.** *Test:* move one edge from `P(B|A) = 0.6` to `0.45` and see whether the headline conclusion flips. If it does and the UI never flagged that edge as load-bearing, the audit story is broken. Any figure past two significant digits is theatre.
8. **Non-falsifiable nodes.** *Test:* sample 10 generated nodes and apply the clarity test — date, source, judgement-free resolution — and record the failure fraction. Then check whether any resolved outcome is written back and scored. A tool that never scores itself cannot claim rigor.

## (c) What NOT to build

- **Causal discovery from data** and **do-calculus identification machinery.** No dataset; the structure is stipulated. Backdoor adjustment on an elicited graph is ceremony.
- **Credal sets / imprecise probability.** Costly, vacuous, uninterpretable.
- **General hybrid continuous BNs.** Thresholded quantities plus noisy-MAX cover the financial cases.
- **Dynamic Bayesian networks / time-step simulation.** Use dated nodes; a DBN is a different product.
- **Fitting CPTs from market data.** A multi-month project with its own backtest-overfitting failure modes.
- **Large auto-generated graphs (100+ nodes).** The value is the audit, not the sprawl. Cap near 30.
- **MCMC/Gibbs, junction-tree compilation, approximate-inference research.** Unneeded at this scale.
- **Rung-3 claims about resolved history** without an explicit SCM and a "model-dependent" label.
- **A chat agent that answers the question directly.** The graph must be the artefact; a chatbot that emits a probability reintroduces every pathology in §3.

---

---

## 1. What the inspiration sources signal

**Metaculus** — an event is not a phrase, it is a *resolvable proposition*. A question is title + background + **resolution criteria** + fine print + dates, and the criteria are load-bearing: they *"should stand on its own as a set of self-contained instructions"* and supersede the background ([FAQ](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/)). Fine print is a deliberate readability valve; questions pass an [approval checklist](https://www.metaculus.com/help/question-checklist/) before going live, because an ambiguous criterion poisons every forecast attached to it.

The relevant primitive is the **Conditional Pair**: "if the Parent resolves Yes, how does the Child resolve?" and "if No?", asked together. In the feed each Parent outcome is an **arrow** and each conditional probability a **bar** — a two-branch fork glyph; in the forecasting UI it is a table, or `IF YES` / `IF NO` buttons opening distribution editors. It exists because *"two forecasters could have the same forecasts… while having very different mental models of their relationship"* ([announcement](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nQhmiKeYPvFaEZfWc/metaculus-introduces-new-conditional-pair-forecast-questions)). **The gap between branches *is* the causal claim** — the unit of value is P(B|A) − P(B|¬A), not P(B|A). One more detail worth copying: when the Parent resolves, the losing branch is **annulled, not scored**. Counterfactual worlds should be visibly *retired*, never silently deleted.

**FutureSearch** — a ReAct research agent over live web search, benchmarked publicly ([Deep Research Bench](https://futuresearch.ai/deep-research-bench/)). Its product supports binary, numeric, date, categorical, thresholded, **conditional** and **decision** forecasts. Two details matter. For conditionals: *"Both branches are forecast together, so the estimates share one coherent view of how A bears on B."* And an explicit line: *"If A is a choice you control, use decision instead"* — conditional is **correlational**, decision is **causal** ([FORECAST docs](https://futuresearch.ai/docs/reference/FORECAST/)).

**ACX, "The AI Superforecasters Are Here"** — Scott Alexander watches FutureSearch deploy three subagents, read 16 websites in two minutes, cite **212 sources**, and answer in five minutes for $8; systems "break complex questions into conjunctive chains." Bots are near elite-human parity and *strongest in finance* ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)). The named failure modes: out-of-distribution events, weak resolution criteria, and FutureSearch's own finding that agents **"extrapolate base rates without checking whether the generating mechanism is still active."** Preseen's backer sets the bar: an LLM *"will happily give you a confident number with nothing underneath it"* ([thread](https://x.com/adityaag/status/2082992027273416882)).

**Net signal:** Catalyst wants *numbers with something underneath them*, expressed as **deltas between worlds**, with resolution-criteria discipline on every node.

---

## 2. Prior art: what to steal, what to avoid

The best "change an input, see downstream effects" design in existence is Vensim's **SyntheSim**: it auto-generates a slider for every constant *and* superimposes a live sparkline on every variable **directly on the model diagram**; dragging re-simulates instantly with the pre-drag run **ghosted behind** ([Vensim](https://www.vensim.com/documentation/synthesim.html)). Bayesian-network GUIs supply the evidence idiom: each node renders a **bar chart of its marginal inside the node box**; click a state to clamp evidence and every other node's bars jump ([Netica](https://www.norsys.com/netica.html)). GeNIe adds whole-graph **sensitivity shading** against a chosen target — red nodes matter, grey have zero influence — with tornado diagrams as drill-down, while candidly admitting sensitivity analysis *"is essentially an art"* ([GeNIe](https://support.bayesfusion.com/docs/GeNIe/bn_sensitivitybn.html)). AgenaRisk overlays **named scenarios on one chart**; BayesiaLab ranks *which unknown to resolve next* by value of information. # PART 1 — research-A: Eliciting numbers from a language model

File: `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/review2/research-A-probability-epistemics.md`

## 1A. The empirical framing (§3 preamble, lines 47)

> "The empirical picture: scaffolded, retrieval-augmented LLMs approach crowd-aggregate accuracy ([Halawi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563)), and LLM *ensembles* are statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd on small question sets ([Schoenegger et al., Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adp1528)) — but on a leakage-free, continuously-refreshed benchmark superforecasters still beat the best LLM by Brier 0.068 vs 0.119 ([ForecastBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19839)), several times the GPT-4→GPT-4o gap. The popular read ([ACX](https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are-here)) is that scaffolds are worth about a model generation and finance-adjacent questions are where AI does relatively *best*. Encouraging — but the scaffold is doing the work, not the model."

Numbers with citations: Brier **0.068** (superforecasters) vs **0.119** (best LLM), ForecastBench (arXiv 2409.19839). Qualifier attached: "statistically indistinguishable from a human crowd **on small question sets**"; ForecastBench is "**leakage-free, continuously-refreshed**" — i.e. the author is explicitly weighting the leakage-free benchmark above the parity results.

## 1B. Base rate first, then adjust (§3, item 1, line 51)

> "**Base rate before narrative.** Elicit the reference class and its historical frequency in a *separate call that has not seen the scenario*, then adjust in a second call. Merging them invites representativeness: a vivid chain scores high because it is a good *story*."

Key operational detail: **two separate calls**, and the base-rate call must **not have seen the scenario**. No citation attached to this item (the supporting literature is representativeness/Kahneman, invoked by name only).

## 1C. Conditionals, never joints (§3, item 2, line 52)

> "**Elicit conditionals, never joints.** Ask for `P(B|A)` and `P(B|¬A)`; compute the rest. Humans and LLMs both violate the conjunction rule — a detailed conjunction is judged *more* likely than its own conjunct ([Tversky & Kahneman 1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunction_fallacy)). A five-step chain at 0.8 per step is 0.33, and the model will call it "very likely" if allowed."

Worked number: **0.8^5 = 0.33** for a five-step chain. Citation: Tversky & Kahneman 1983 (linked to the Wikipedia conjunction-fallacy page, not the paper).

## 1D. Small ensembles, k samples, geometric mean of odds, dispersion (§3, item 3, line 53)

> "**Sample k ≥ 5 times** across prompt variants and ideally two model families, then **aggregate by geometric mean of odds** ([summary](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/sMjcjnnpoAQCcedL2/when-pooling-forecasts-use-the-geometric-mean-of-odds)). **Keep the spread**: dispersion across independent elicitations is a defensible first-order estimate of that parameter's uncertainty, feeding §4 at zero extra cost."

Three separable claims: (a) **k ≥ 5**, varied over **prompt variants** and **ideally two model families**; (b) aggregate by **geometric mean of odds**; (c) **retain the dispersion** as the parameter's uncertainty.

Note on evidentiary status: the geometric-mean-of-odds link is an **EA Forum post** ("summary"), not a peer-reviewed source. **`k ≥ 5` carries no citation** — it is the author's judgement. Median and arithmetic mean are **not discussed anywhere in the document**; geometric mean of odds is asserted as the aggregator without a stated comparison against the alternatives. This is a gap if the parent agent expected a median-vs-geomean-vs-arithmetic argument.

## 1E. Do not extremize (§3, item 4, line 54)

> "**Do not extremize by default.** Extremizing helps for independent human forecasters ([discussion](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/biL94PKfeHmgHY6qe/principled-extremizing-of-aggregated-forecasts)), but LLM samples are highly correlated and chain errors compound multiplicatively. Here it manufactures confidence."

The stated reason extremizing transfers badly: **LLM samples are highly correlated** (violating the independence premise) **and** chain errors **compound multiplicatively**. Citation is again an EA Forum post, and it is cited *for the positive result in humans*, i.e. the document's own recommendation runs against its cited source, on an uncited mechanistic argument.

## 1F. Known LLM pathologies / calibration correction (§3, item 5, line 55)

> "**Correct known LLM pathologies**: RLHF pushes models toward confident-sounding outputs ([Taming Overconfidence in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09724)), and verbalized probabilities cluster on round numbers and avoid the tails. Force explicit `<1%` / `>99%` options; add a per-model recalibration map once questions resolve."

Two concrete mechanisms: **forced `<1%` / `>99%` response options**, and a **per-model recalibration map built from resolved questions**. Citation covers only the RLHF-overconfidence half; the **round-number clustering / tail avoidance claim is uncited inline** (`Just Ask for Calibration`, arXiv 2305.14975, appears only in the source list at line 163, never invoked in the body).

## 1G. Coherence / consistency checks (§3, lines 57–62)

> "**Coherence checks to run automatically** (all cheap, all blocking):
>
> - Marginal consistency: `P(B) ≈ P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|¬A)P(¬A)` vs. a directly-elicited `P(B)`; flag >10pp divergence.
> - Relevance: an edge is justified only if `P(B|A) ≠ P(B|¬A)`. Equal values → delete the edge.
> - Symmetry of dependence: `P(B|A) > P(B)` iff `P(A|B) > P(A)`.
> - Chain sanity: compare the model's *verbal* summary ("highly likely") against the computed number and show the conflict. This is the anti-conjunction-fallacy feature, and a genuinely good product moment."

All four are **blocking**, not advisory. The threshold **>10pp** is uncited/author-chosen. Note the fourth check is framed as both a rigor mechanism and **a product moment** — verbal-vs-computed conflict surfaced to the user.

## 1H. Elicitation units — odds ratios, not probabilities (§2, line 39)

> "**Recommendation: signed log-odds as the default, with leaky noisy-OR and noisy-AND per node.** It handles inhibition, which noisy-OR cannot; elicitation is in odds ratios ("~3× more likely"), which forecasters can produce; each edge's contribution is `wᵢ` in bits, so the inspector gets "this edge moved the target +1.2 bits" free…"

Directly relevant to elicitation design: ask the model for a **signed odds ratio ("~3× more likely")**, not a raw probability. Parameter counts: logistic link = **`k + 1` numbers** (line 37); leaky noisy-OR = **`k + 1` numbers** (line 34); full CPT = **`2^k` rows, 16 numbers at k = 4** (line 32), elicited from "a model that will produce non-monotone, mutually incoherent rows."

Also from §2 (line 41), a constraint on elicited numbers: "**saturation** (clip and warn past ~0.99)."

## 1I. Dispersion → a range, not a point (§4, line 70)

> "**Monte Carlo over parameters → a band, not a point.** Draw each parameter from its across-sample dispersion (§3.3) ~1,000 times and re-run inference. ~20 lines, and the strongest antidote to false precision: the band visibly widens with chain length, which is the honest lesson."

**~1,000 draws**, parameter distributions sourced directly from the k-sample spread of §3.3. Explicitly rejected alternative (line 75):

> "**Skip imprecise probability / credal networks.** Interval propagation is exponential in practice, the intervals go vacuously wide, and no user can interpret them. Parameter MC captures ~90% of the honesty at ~5% of the cost."

The **~90% / ~5%** figures are rhetorical, uncited.

Related, §4 item 2 (line 71): "**One-way sensitivity / tornado.** Perturb each parameter over its plausible range, rank by target movement… `2 × #params` inferences — milliseconds here. Tells the user *which single number their thesis rests on*."

## 1J. Base rates as leak terms — elicited, never defaulted (§5, line 87)

> "**Structural uncertainty is the dominant error term, and the leak is where it lives.** Every node's "no parents active" probability must be *elicited as a base rate*, never defaulted to zero; a zero leak asserts the LLM's cause list is exhaustive, which it never is. Disclose per graph that the computed number is a lower bound if the enumerated causes are only some of the causes."

## 1K. Provenance of raw samples — keeping the k (§6, line 95)

> "**Provenance per node and edge**: source URLs with retrieval timestamps, model, prompt version, elicitation method, and the k raw samples *before* aggregation. Without the raw samples you cannot distinguish "the model was confident" from "the models disagreed and we averaged"."

## 1L. Calibration and scoring (§6, lines 96–99)

> "**Immutable snapshots.** Every published chain is frozen and timestamped so it can be scored later. A forecast you can silently edit is not a forecast."

> "**Proper scoring rules.** Brier for the user-facing calibration view; log score alongside, since it punishes confident errors — the failure mode that matters here. Always report a **skill score** relative to the elicited base rate; absolute Brier on easy questions flatters everyone."

> "**Metaculus** — an event is not a phrase, it is a *resolvable proposition*. > "The relevant primitive is the **Conditional Pair**: "if the Parent resolves Yes, how does the Child resolve?" and "if No?", asked together.
